# Northfield Analytics joins Example Lab to work on evaluation tooling | Example Lab

Northfield Analytics joins Example Lab to work on evaluation tooling
A small team with a long record of building careful benchmarks.
Good evaluations are slow to build and easy to get wrong, and the teams that do them well are rare. Northfield Analytics has spent four years writing test suites that check not only whether a model answers correctly but whether it answers for the right reasons, and their tools are already used by several research groups to audit their own results.
Starting this month, the Northfield team joins Example Lab. Their open-source harness will stay open, and its maintainers will keep reviewing outside contributions as before. Within the lab, the team will lead work on evaluations that run continuously during training rather than once at the end, so that regressions show up while they are still cheap to fix.
“We built Northfield because we kept finding results we could not reproduce,” said Hanne Rosvold, the team's founder. “Joining a lab that trains models lets us test our ideas where the stakes are highest, and we intend to keep publishing what we learn.”
“Evaluation is where research turns into evidence,” said Teodor Malakai, who leads research at Example Lab. “The Northfield team has shown that it is possible to be rigorous and practical at the same time, and we are glad to have them.”
We will share the first results of the joint work in the coming months.
Disclosure: one member of the Example Lab board was an early adviser to Northfield Analytics and took no part in the decision.
